## Description

[](https://github.com/pcheek1991)

[pcheek1991](https://github.com/pcheek1991)

opened [on Aug 27, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17549#issue-5270378235)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

On Windows 11, yt-dlp silently replaces the ASCII forward slash "/" (U+002F SOLIDUS) in metadata used by an output template with U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS.

The source title is:

Process serving Firestone (and/or)(or/and) Bridgestone on behalf of USAA per Patrick Jenks

The filename generated by yt-dlp contains:

Process serving Firestone (and[U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS]or)(or[U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS]and) Bridgestone on behalf of USAA per Patrick Jenks

Environment:

Windows 11  
yt-dlp master@2026.08.26.234438  
commit [`94eba4c`](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/94eba4c156af080e87caf10cf8ffbea03bd17407)  
win_exe  
locale cp1252  
filesystem encoding utf-8  
output encoding utf-8

The behavior reproduces both when printing the generated filename and during an actual successful HLS download.

This is not an extractor failure. The source metadata contains the normal ASCII "/" character. The substitution occurs when yt-dlp constructs a filesystem-safe filename.

The substitution is problematic because U+29F8 is visually similar to "/" but is a different Unicode character. In a downstream Windows PowerShell 5.1 workflow, the UTF-8 bytes for U+29F8 were interpreted using a legacy Windows encoding and appeared as the mojibake sequence "a-section-sign-cedilla" rather than the intended character.

I understand that "/" cannot be used literally inside a Windows filename. The issue is the silent substitution with a Unicode lookalike rather than an ASCII-safe replacement, and the lack of an obvious warning or documentation describing this transformation.

Expected behavior:

Either clearly document the filename sanitization transformation from U+002F to U+29F8, warn when the substitution occurs, or provide a clearly documented ASCII-safe filename sanitization behavior for Windows.

Actual behavior:

ASCII U+002F "/" in the source title is silently transformed into U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS in the generated filename.

The transformation also occurs with --skip-download and --print filename, demonstrating that it occurs in filename generation rather than during HLS downloading, ffmpeg processing, or filesystem writing.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

This is somewhat documented in <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#differences-in-default-behavior> :

>      * yt-dlp's sanitization of invalid characters in filenames is different/smarter than in youtube-dl. You can use `--compat-options filename-sanitization` to revert to youtube-dl's behavior

...and also in the "Usage and Options" section of the README / `--help` output / man page:
    
    --restrict-filenames            Restrict filenames to only ASCII characters,
                                    and avoid "&" and spaces in filenames
    --no-restrict-filenames         Allow Unicode characters, "&" and spaces in
                                    filenames (default)
    --windows-filenames             Force filenames to be Windows-compatible
    --no-windows-filenames          Sanitize filenames only minimally
    

> or provide a clearly documented ASCII-safe filename sanitization behavior for Windows.

I think `--restrict-filenames` is what you're looking for.

Or else you can override the default sanitization with your own using `--replace-in-metadata`:
    
    --replace-in-metadata [WHEN:]FIELDS REGEX REPLACE
                                    Replace text in a metadata field using the
                                    given regex. This option can be used
                                    multiple times. Supported values of "WHEN"
                                    are the same as that of --use-postprocessor
                                    (default: pre_process)

  6. ### pcheek1991 commented on Aug 31, 2026

[](/pcheek1991)

[pcheek1991](/pcheek1991)

[on Aug 31, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17549#issuecomment-5485592575)

Author

More actions

Thank you. I want to distinguish a workaround from an explanation. `--restrict-filenames` and `--replace-in-metadata` do not resolve the reported problem. They require the user to alter otherwise valid source metadata or accept a different filename policy to avoid an undocumented default substitution.

Windows requires the literal `/` to be replaced because it is a path separator. Windows does not require its replacement with U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS. The only technical advantage I can identify is that `⧸` visually resembles `/` and preserves more information than replacing several reserved characters with the same underscore. That may also reduce filename collisions. However, I found no documentation or source comment explaining that design decision or why U+29F8 was chosen specifically. The tradeoff is that yt-dlp silently inserts a non-ASCII character into an otherwise ASCII title, creating compatibility problems for older or legacy-encoded downstream tools.

In ordinary language, the resulting “mojibake” means garbled text: one program wrote the Unicode character using one character codebook, while another program read those bytes using the wrong codebook. The downstream program produced the visible garbage, but yt-dlp introduced the unexpected Unicode character that triggered the incompatibility.

The substitution is explicitly programmed at [`yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py`, lines 644–646](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/bbc809a1161d3bfca51fa36f59dda35556ee85a0/yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py#L644-L646):
         
         elif is_id is NO_DEFAULT and not restricted and char in '"*:<>?|/\\':
             # Replace with their full-width unicode counterparts
             return {'/': '\u29F8', '\\': '\u29f9'}.get(char, chr(ord(char) + 0xfee0))

The comment is technically inaccurate: U+29F8 is BIG SOLIDUS, not U+FF0F FULLWIDTH SOLIDUS.

The minimally sanitized non-Windows path independently performs the same replacement at [`yt_dlp/YoutubeDL.py`, lines 1398–1401](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/bbc809a1161d3bfca51fa36f59dda35556ee85a0/yt_dlp/YoutubeDL.py#L1398-L1401):
         
         def sanitize(key, value):
             return str(value).replace('/', '\u29F8').replace('\0', '')

The behavior is enforced by tests at [`test/test_utils.py`, lines 161–164](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/bbc809a1161d3bfca51fa36f59dda35556ee85a0/test/test_utils.py#L161-L164) and [`test/test_YoutubeDL.py`, lines 697–703](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/bbc809a1161d3bfca51fa36f59dda35556ee85a0/test/test_YoutubeDL.py#L697-L703).

I could not find user-facing documentation identifying the U+002F-to-U+29F8 transformation. [`README.md`, lines 668–673](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/bbc809a1161d3bfca51fa36f59dda35556ee85a0/README.md#L668-L673) describes the options only generally, while [`README.md`, line 2339](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/bbc809a1161d3bfca51fa36f59dda35556ee85a0/README.md#L2339) calls the behavior “different/smarter” without identifying the transformation. Open issue [[#8962](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8962)]([#8962](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8962)) documents substantially similar confusion.

A focused patch could:

     1. Correct the inaccurate comment in `yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py`.
     2. Document the exact U+002F `/` to U+29F8 `⧸` mapping and its compatibility tradeoff.
     3. Clarify that character restrictions, platform/path compatibility, and legacy sanitizer compatibility are separate policies.
     4. Explain that macOS may impose additional filesystem Unicode-version constraints.
     5. Consider an ASCII-safe or user-selectable substitution policy that does not require altering the source metadata.

  11. ### Lieutenant-L-T-Smash commented on Sep 1, 2026

> but yt-dlp introduced the unexpected Unicode character that triggered the incompatibility.

yt-dlp has to do _something_ with the illegal character. The title must already be presumed to be Unicode. There is no guarantee that it's restricted to ASCII, either before or after sanitiziation, unless using `--restrict-filenames` which explicitly guarantees that. What would you propose doing if the original video title included a U+29F8?

If your downstream program can only handle ASCII, then that is the option you must use.

> ASCII only (7-bit?

ASCII is 7-bit by definition. Calling an 8-bit code "ASCII" is an error.

# Spotify podcasts with passthrough enabled #17528

## Description

[](https://github.com/cnotin)

[cnotin](https://github.com/cnotin)

opened [on Aug 24, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17528#issue-5239993747)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting a new site support request
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that none of provided URLs [violate any copyrights](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#is-the-website-primarily-used-for-piracy) or contain any [DRM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_rights_management) to the best of my knowledge
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and am willing to share it if required



### Region

_No response_

### Example URLs

  * Podcast show: <https://open.spotify.com/show/2IyZviDs8WLsVzCNamqhc2>
  * Podcast episode: <https://open.spotify.com/episode/45m6z2GQIIvert8LxSXcjt> -> <https://open.spotify.com/embed/episode/45m6z2GQIIvert8LxSXcjt>



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Most Spotify podcasts cannot be downloaded, or are DRM protected, hence the current blocking of its domain: 

[yt-dlp/yt_dlp/extractor/unsupported.py](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/81ecd58b1394793e6da9998cc19fdb45657f1685/yt_dlp/extractor/unsupported.py#L34)

Line 34 in [81ecd58](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/81ecd58b1394793e6da9998cc19fdb45657f1685)

|  r'open\\.spotify\\.com',   
---|---  
  
However, the corresponding embed page for a podcast episode, sometimes contain the true URL of the file. For example, if you look at the HTML of <https://open.spotify.com/embed/episode/45m6z2GQIIvert8LxSXcjt>, you'll notice this:
    
    
    "passthrough":"ALLOWED","passthroughUrl":"https://traffic.megaphone.fm/GLT2458722524.mp3?updated=1670807113"
    

And indeed it points to a non-DRM MP3 file that can be downloaded.

Therefore, I suggest that, when `"passthrough":"ALLOWED"`, to offer downloading.

Here's a counter-example, for example this episode from a different Spotify podcast: <https://open.spotify.com/embed/episode/0DJKSCskUdVXJca83MsW53> which lacks passthrough:
    
    
    "passthrough":"NONE","passthroughUrl":""
    

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

    > yt-dlp -vU https://open.spotify.com/show/2IyZviDs8WLsVzCNamqhc2

## Description

[](https://github.com/pukkandan)

[pukkandan](https://github.com/pukkandan)

opened [on May 17, 2022](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766#issue-1238299309)

Issue body actions

Some known common issues. Make sure to always check this before opening issues. **Duplicates of these will be strictly treated as spam!**

**Useful issue tracker filters:**

[[Core Issues]](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement%2Cbug%2Ccore%3Adownloader%2Ccore%3Apost-processor%2Ccore%3Aextractor%2Ccore%3Anetworking%2Ccore%3Acookies) [[Site Issues]](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Asite-request%2Csite-enhancement%2Csite-bug) [[YouTube issues]](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Asite%3Ayoutube) [[Good issues for new devs]](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3A%22gateway-issue%22)

## High priority issues

  * **[[Youtube] ERROR: Video unavailable. Playback on other websites has been disabled by the video owner (web_embedded player response playability status: UNPLAYABLE) #17497](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17497)**
  * **[[Youtube] ERROR: The page needs to be reloaded (tv_downgraded player response playability status: UNPLAYABLE) #17389](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17389)**
  * [[Youtube] Only format 18 (360p) is available for age-restricted videos #17542](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17542)



## Intractable issues

  * **[[YouTube] This content isn't available, try again later. #11426](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11426)**
    * You are exceeding the rate limit. Refer to [the wiki on how to avoid](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors#this-content-isnt-available-try-again-later).
  * **[Passing Youtube cookies doesn't seem to work; cookies are being invalidated quickly #8227](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8227)**
    * [How to effectively export YouTube cookies](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors#exporting-youtube-cookies)
  * **[[youtube] Sign in to confirm you’re not a bot #10128](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10128)**
    * Your IP has been blocked by YouTube while you are logged out. You can [pass logged-in cookies](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors#exporting-youtube-cookies); however, doing so may get your account blocked. The safer solution is to use a different IP.
    * To prevent this, [try using a PO Token provider](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/PO-Token-Guide), though it will not help if your IP is already blocked.
  * **[[youtube] "Video unavailable" with cookies - YouTube blocking accounts from web #10085](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10085)**
    * Your account has been blocked by YouTube, or the video is not available in your region.
    * Avoid passing cookies, or add a [sleep delay](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#workarounds) to each download.
  * **[[Youtube] Immediate HTTP Error 403 on download #11868](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11868)**
    * Try using `--force-ipv4`, try using yt-dlp from a different IP address (e.g. disable your VPN), try using logged-in cookies if you were using yt-dlp logged-out, or try using yt-dlp without cookies if you were using logged-in cookies

# External issues

  * **[[Youtube] HTTP Error 403 when using bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider plugin #17368](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17368)**
  * [ffmpeg can't seek in Youtube's iOS m3u8 streams / `--download-sections` only downloads audio #9552](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9552)
    * Use `-S proto:https` or `--extractor-args "youtube:player_client=default,-ios"`
  * [`--cookies-from-browser` "Permission denied" errors when Chrome/chromium-based browser is open in Windows #7271](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7271)
    * Try after closing chrome completely OR
    * Launch chrome from command line w/ `chrome.exe --disable-features=LockProfileCookieDatabase`
    * Alternatively, you can [install](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#installing-plugins) the [ChomeCookieUnlock yt-dlp plugin](https://github.com/seproDev/yt-dlp-ChromeCookieUnlock)
  * [`--cookies-from-browser`: WARNING: failed to decrypt with DPAPI / ERROR: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'decode' #10927](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10927)
  * [[youtube] Is downloading a livestream in 1440p or 2160p no longer available? #11262](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11262)
  * [[Youtube] 8k VR180 SBS videos no longer available #9903](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9903)
    * Use `--extractor-arg "youtube:player_client=android_vr,default"`
  * [[Youtube] throttling and inconsistent speed in Russia #10443](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10443)
    * [Workarounds](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10443#issuecomment-2248940967)
  * [[Discord bot] Music stops in the middle #8854](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8854)
  * [[youtube] Endless "Incomplete data received" when downloading playlist #10394](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10394)
    * Don't use `--extractor-retries infinite`
  * [FFMPEG "Invalid data found when processing input" on live/post-live/dash videos (duplicate ftyp) #8641](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8641)
    * Regression in ffmpeg 6.1. Upgrade to ffmpeg 6.1.1 or to [master build](https://github.com/yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds/releases) revision `N-112916` or later
  * [[youtube] "Invalid data found when processing input" / ffmpeg errors on HDR VP9 in mp4 #7541](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7541)
    * ffmpeg bug. Upgrade to ffmpeg 7.0.1 or to the latest [master build](https://github.com/yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds/releases)
  * [`--mark-watched` fails with urlopen error #8149](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8149)
    * Disable pi-hole or whitelist `s.youtube.com`
  * [Chapter Embedding Results in Unnamed Chapters When Using Recent FFmpeg Builds #6859](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6859)
    * ffmpeg regression. Use <https://github.com/yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds> or upgrade to 6.1.1 or newer
  * [yt-dlp is detected as a virus #25](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/25)
    * It's a false positive. Complain to your vendor. There is nothing we can do
  * [Incomplete Data Recieved #1787](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1787)
    * Broken from Youtube's side. If downloading comments, use `-i` to ignore the error
  * [Wrong year in metadata in M4A, MP4, FLAC format #3087](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3087)
    * Workaround: `--parse-metadata "%(release_year,upload_date).4s:(?P<meta_date>.+)"`
  * [pyinstaller temp files are not cleaned up when using yt-dlp.exe with mpv #10294](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10294)
  * [Long Start-Up Time for `yt-dlp_macos` #10425](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10425)
  * [`--download-sections` / ffmpeg fails to seek in a 26+ hour long Twitch m3u8 #5372](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5372)
  * [Using proxy and `--download-sections`/ ffmpeg fails with HTTP Error 400/401/403 #12915](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12915)



# FAQ

See <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ>

  * **[How to avoid Youtube's new "Super Resolution" AI-upscaled formats #15325](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15325)**
  * **[Getting deno to work in Termux. #15095 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15095#issuecomment-3544324838)**
    * Run a full Termux upgrade with `pkg update && pkg upgrade` before `pkg install deno`
  * **[[YouTube] Enhanced bitrate no longer available to download? #14133 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14133#issuecomment-3217679575)**
  * [**Filename too long**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1136#issuecomment-932077195)
    * Use `-o "%(title).150B [%(id)s].%(ext)s"`
  * **[[YouTube]`--write-comments`: "Incomplete data received. Giving up after 3 retries" warnings #15435](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15435)**
  * **[twitter: No video could be found in this tweet #14742](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14742)**
  * [[Question] odd ba* format selection? #979 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/979#issuecomment-919629354)
    * Generally do not use `ba*`
  * [Fix playlist_index's inconsistent behavior #302](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/302)
    * Check `playlist_autonumber` and `--compat-option playlist-index`
  * [yt-dlp python module not compiling with pyinstaller #3845](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3845)
    * Use `bundle/pyinstaller.py`
  * [Subtitle file is not deleted after being embedded #630 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/630#issuecomment-893659460)
    * Use `--compat-option no-keep-subs`
  * [`--download-sections`/`--sponsorblock-remove` does not cut at exact point #4216](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4216) / [YouTube Clip Downloads have unintented extra beginning part with no video #5080](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5080)
    * Use `--force-keyframes-at-cuts`
  * [Duplicating pull request from youtube-dl to yt-dlp #4202](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4202)
  * [How to check in browser if the video is DRM protected](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4062#issuecomment-1153474056)
  * [\--cookies-from-browser for a chrome/firefox like browser or non-default install location #2903](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/2903)
  * [What are yt-dlp's error codes? #4262 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4262#issuecomment-1173133105)
  * [Extractor option `language` for `crunchyrollbeta` #4640](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4640)
  * [Ability to strip Emoji from downloaded file  #4836](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4836) / [File names use "full-width" special characters: '？' vs '?' #5014](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5014)
  * [[Youtube] Extract exact timestamps #1803](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1803)
  * [[Feature Request] Crop to square thumbnail when embedding in MP3s #429 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/429#issuecomment-2282554440)
  * Download only videos with subtitles 
    * `--parse-metadata "%(subtitles.\:.0.ext|)s:^(?!\[\])(?P<has_subs>.)" -v --match-filter has_subs`
  * [How do I rename previously-downloaded files with nothing but the youtube video ID? #5692](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5692)
  * Remove specific fields from info-json - [[Suggestion] Redact `formats` in info json with an option #455 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/455#issuecomment-1367741786)
  * About subtitles in mp4 container - [Convert webvtt subtitles in mp4 into useable format #5833 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5833#issuecomment-1358246240)
  * [Find the API option for a CLI argument #5859 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5859#issuecomment-1363938900)
    * Use <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/devscripts/cli_to_api.py>
  * [[YouTube] `youtube:skip=translated_subs` doesn't work for some videos. #3875](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3875)
  * [Youtube bestvideo and vp9 preference. #1232 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1232#issuecomment-939635345)
  * [repo: git log broken by SSH signature #7322](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7322)
  * [download comments into separate comments.json file #2372 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/2372#issuecomment-1506413976)
  * [How to force a conversion to a specific video codec? #7607 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7607#issuecomment-1636960750)
  * [How to download youtube videos in mp4 format? #8880](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8880)

  * [[youtube] 256kbps music formats not being extracted #12455 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12455#issuecomment-2677077342)
  * [[PYI-12704:ERROR] Failed to extract Cryptodome\Cipher_ARC4.pyd: decompression resulted in return code -1! #16522](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16522)
    * You probably don't have enough free disk space on the drive where your temp dir is located

More actions

> 3\. That will work for this podcast. But is this a general solution?

nope, on some pages, which contain `&quot;`, the `get_element_by_id` call can break the json:  
`>>> get_element_by_id('preloads-json','<script id="preloads-json">{"testkey":"test&quot;val"}</script>')`  
is:  
`'{"testkey":"test"val"}'`  
should:  
`'{"testkey":"test&quot;val"}'`

edit:  
since `clean_html` also breaks it in the same way, I've copied a line from it, and this seems to work:  
`re.sub('<.*?>', '', get_element_html_by_id('preloads-json','...'))`

  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Italy

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I have noticed that sometimes, when downloading songs on Soundcloud, yt-dlp does not find the "Premium" hls_aac_256k stream.  
I am not talking about DRM-protected songs.  
I do have Soundcloud GO+ and I am correctly passing cookies from Firefox (and was also able to reproduce the bug with cookies from file in netscape format).  
As an example, here's two tracks:  
This one works correctly: <https://soundcloud.com/moskalus/premiere-easygoingtech-reassembly-lulo-rcrds>  
This one does not: <https://soundcloud.com/lulo-604301027/8e3bb12c-b534-4e7a-a577-4e51b5e42741>

The hls_aac_256k stream actually exists, since I can download it by pasting the requested playlist.m3u8 URL that appears in the network tools in Chrome with a command like  
yt-dlp "<https://cf-hls-aac-media.sndcdn.com/playlist/8d0af2a5-31f1-4269-8f2d-fbff04a51f22.m4a/playlist.m3u8?bunch_of_query_parameters>" -o "filename.m4a" --cookies-from-browser firefox  
(And I can confirm it works with spectral analysis tools like spek)

What I noticed is that the playlist.m3u8 file for the working song starts with:  
#EXTM3U  
#EXT-X-VERSION:7  
#EXT-X-TARGETDURATION:10  
#EXT-X-MEDIA-SEQUENCE:0  
#EXT-X-PLAYLIST-TYPE:VOD

And the playlist.m3u8 file for the not working song starts with:  
#EXTM3U  
#EXT-X-VERSION:6  
#EXT-X-PLAYLIST-TYPE:VOD  
#EXT-X-TARGETDURATION:10  
#EXT-X-MEDIA-SEQUENCE:0

I attached sample playlist.m3u8 files for both cases. I replaced all token and strings that might be sensitive with some capslocked keywords like POLICY, SIGNATURE and KEY_PAIR.  
I don't know if it's relevant but in the bugged playlist.m3u8 file the POLICY and SIGNATURE in the first URL are different from the rest of the URLs. This does not happen in the working playlist file.  
I tried to highlight it with  
?Policy=POLICY1:POLICY2  
?Policy=POLICY1:POLICY3  
The first part is the same for both (it was some base64 encoded string), then the second part differs. Interpret the ":" here as a concatenation, there was no actual ":" char between the two parts of the policy token/string.  
I also used SIGNATURE1 and SIGNATURE2 to highlight the difference in signatures.

[bugged_playlist.m3u8.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34103248/bugged_playlist.m3u8.txt)  
[working_playlist.m3u8.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34103247/working_playlist.m3u8.txt)

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

This disturbingly long playlist is generated by combining `entries` found in the page, a dict mapping `original` to `{'track': track_title}`, with `files` items from a JSON metadata API, each a dict with some keys that might link to an `entry`.

Thus: ...
         
         # entries
         {
             '001. [S01.E01] - Edward and Gordon.mpg': {'track': '001. [S01.E01] - Edward and Gordon'},
             ...
             '004. S01 Ep04 - Thomas and Gordon.mp4': 
           {'track': '004. S01 Ep04 - Thomas and Gordon'},
             ...
         }
         # files
         [{'crc32': '088b3efc',
           'format': 'h.264',
           'height': '480',
           'length': '332.96',
           'md5': '324249dccbc09c2d3dd0242612631e8d',
           'mtime': '1781345455',
           'name': '001. [S01.E01] - Edward and Gordon.mp4',
           'original': '001. [S01.E01] - Edward and Gordon.mpg',
           'sha1': '94a7b06d7b61008861090252511f3545db0e485a',
           'size': '33697154',
           'source': 'derivative',
           'width': '640'},
          {'crc32': 'efdc1a86',
           'format': 'MPEG2',
           'height': '576',
           'length': '332.96',
           'md5': '92dbca8fd12cfb367d7e29113f500a8e',
           'mtime': '1781332432',
           'name': '001. [S01.E01] - Edward and Gordon.mpg',
           'sha1': '79427a0beb072198f996fd110f9713ccc7b95b91',
           'size': '281833476',
           'source': 'original',
           'width': '768'},
           ...
          {'crc32': '4749769f',
           'format': 'h.264 IA',
           'height': '480',
           'length': '332.4',
           'md5': '181aabe7d94deb8a344212853e80e56a',
           'mtime': '1767719691',
           'name': '004. S01 Ep04 - Thomas and Gordon.ia.mp4',
           'original': '004. S01 Ep04 - Thomas and Gordon.mp4',
           'sha1': '2557fdcfef34229f354bd936efb44a4bae5b3683',
           'size': '33645039',
           'source': 'derivative',
           'width': '640'},
           ...
         ]

The entry `id` is only set when a `files` item has a `name` that matches the entry's key. In item 4, it doesn't, so an error is raised as in the log. There are 611 entries but only 498 `file` items with `['source'] == 'original'`, whose `name` will match, so 123 are going to fail.

Making the extractor match the `original` (if present) when `['source'] != 'original'` and the `name` otherwise fixed item 4 for me (and also made `--flat-playlist --skip-download` work for the whole playlist):
         
         for f in metadata['files']:
         -            if f['name'] in entries:
         -                entries[f['name']] = merge_dicts(entries[f['name']], {
         -                    'id': identifier + '/' + f['name'],
         +            name = (f.get('original') if f.get('source') != 'original' else None) or f['name']
         +            if name in entries:
         +                entries[name] = merge_dicts(entries[name], {
         +                    'id': identifier + '/' + name,
                              **traverse_obj(f, {
                                  'title': (('title', 'original', 'name'), {str}, any),
                                  'display_id': ('name', {str}),
                                  'description': ('description', ({str}, (..., all, {' '.join})), {clean_html}, filter, any),
                                  'creators': ('creator', (None, ...), {str}, filter, all, filter),
                                  'duration': ('length', {parse_duration}),
                                  'track_number': ('track', {int_or_none}),
                                  'album': ('album', {str}),
                                  'discnumber': ('disc', {int_or_none}),
                                  'release_year': ('year', {int_or_none}),
                              }),
                          })
         -                entry = entries[f['name']]
         +                entry = entries[name]
                      elif traverse_obj(f, ('original', {str})) in entries:

_Updated to fix playlist item titles in test`_2`_  
Unrelated, the extractor doesn't seem to be handling playlist item tracks of `kind == 'subtitles'` properly. Shouldn't they be put in `subtitles`? Or am I failing to understand ll.278-283?

Code s/t like this in an extractor works:
         
         next_data = self._search_nextjs_v13_data(webpage, video_id)
                 video = traverse_obj(next_data, (
                     ..., 'data', all, lambda _, v: v['video']['id'] == video_id,
                     'video', any))
                 m3u8_url = traverse_obj(video, 'src')
         
                 return {
                     'id': video_id,
                     **dict(zip(
                         ('formats', 'subtitles'),
                         self._extract_m3u8_formats_and_subtitles(
                             m3u8_url, video_id, 'mp4', fatal=False)
                     )),
                     **traverse_obj(video, {
                         'uploader': 'authorName',
                         'uploader_id': 'authorSlug',
                         'timestamp': ('createdAtIso', {parse_iso8601}),

В прямых эфирах КопеллаЛайф есть возможность, смотреть VOD-записи, если канал без галочки, то запись хранится 7 дней, если канал с галочкой, то запись хранится 30 дней, а затем удаляется безвозратно.

В КопеллеЛайф тоже есть прямые эфиры. <https://copellalive.net/watch?v=ls_240cbd12982c4698b1b3> \- эфир телеканала RUSIK.  
Если провернуть ленту назад, то можно увидеть, записи программ, которые уже были, при нажатии продедшей программы будет воспроизводится запись программы. <https://api.copellalive.net/static/hls/tpa_12250f3810124923ae56a6bb15bc812e/epg-source.m3u8>, также есть и мастер-вариант - запись VOD эфира за определенный промежуток программы.

Когда трансляции нет, отображается заглушка эфира. Она длится определенное количество времени (меньше минуты). На некоторых каналах видеозаглушки вообще нет. При появлении прямого эфира формируется мастер плейлист и index плейлист, который имеет определенное кол-во сегментов. VOD-записи формируются из прямого эфира, и во время прямого эфира можно смотреть и VOD-запись, и текущую программу. <https://live.copellalive.net/> \- ссылка на плейлист прямого эфира.

Все прямые трансляции используются систему хранения Copium и Telegram Bot API. И VOD-записи частично хранятся через CDN Телеграма. Для временнего хранения используются плейлисты типа epg-source. Аудио релизы тоже хранятся в формате HLS. Статичное изображение хранится в видеокодеке H.264 и аудиокодеке AAC-LC. Это статичное изображение используется только для заполнения пространства в веб-плеере КопеллаЛайф.

Также CopellaLive (КопеллаЛайф) имеет радиостанции, но их количество настолько большое, что добавлять их в yt-dlp просто бессмыслено. Даже называть их количество, просто не хочется из-за прикрученной (если так назвать) онлайн библиотеки радиостанций.

(АНГЛИЙСКАЯ ВЕРСИЯ ТЕКСТА ЧЕРЕЗ ОНЛАЙН-ПЕРЕВОДЧИК, ЧАСТИЧНОЕ РЕДАКТИРОВАНИЕ ВРУЧНУЮ)

In live broadcasts of CopellaLive, it is possible to watch VOD recordings, if the channel is unchecked, then the recording is stored for 7 days, if the channel is ticked, then the recording is stored for 30 days, and then permanently deleted.

CopellaLive also has live broadcasts. <https://copellalive.net/watch?v=ls_240cbd12982c4698b1b3> \- broadcast of the RUSIK TV channel.  
If you turn the tape back, you can see the recordings of programs that have already been, when you click on the program that has passed, the recording of the program will be played. <https://api.copellalive.net/static/hls/tpa_12250f3810124923ae56a6bb15bc812e/epg-source.m3u8> there is also a master option - recording the VOD broadcast for a certain period of the program.

When there is no broadcast, the stub of the broadcast is displayed. It lasts a certain amount of time (less than a minute). On some channels, there is no video plug at all. When a live broadcast appears, a master playlist and an index playlist are formed, which has a certain number of segments. VOD recordings are generated from the live broadcast, and during the live broadcast you can watch both the VOD recording and the current program. <https://live.copellalive.net> / - link to the playlist of the live broadcast.

All live broadcasts - they aso use system Copium - for live broadcasts and VOD-videos over Telegram CDN. CopellaLive using Telegram storage and Telegram Bot API - for general video storage and live broadcasts, as well as for temporary storage of VOD recordings of programms. And audio releases have a static image, in H.264 video and AAC-LC audio, and are also stored in HLS format, the picture is only needed in the player to fill the space.

CopellaLive also has radio stations, but their number is so much greater that adding support in yt-dlp is simply useless. I just don't want to even name their number because of the screwed-up (if you can call it that) library of the online world radio stations.

Currently I can't see any live streams: all channels are inactive.

The items in the scroll-bar under the "OFF-LIVE" linked Rusik channel aren't properly linked, but just part of a JS single-page app that constructs the .../tpa... m3u8 links.

Radio stations also don't seem to be properly linked in the site but the recommended station comes from [https://api.copellalive.net/videos?type=radio&limit=10](https://api.copellalive.net/videos?type=radio&limit=10) while the global library comes from <https://api.copellalive.net/radio/library/topclicks?offset=0> and the links there are to <https://radio.garden> (which you might as well use). "Your stations" seems to be wired into the site JS somehow, but maybe this behaves differently if you are logged in.

Current live streams, videos, podcasts and playlists should all be possible to handle.

Additional findings (may point to the root cause):

     1. Naver TV was shut down on 2026-09-30 (Naver announced officially that long-form videos move to "Naver Clip" and live streaming to CHZZK). 
        * <https://www.etnews.com/20260730000281>
     2. tv.naver.com URLs now redirect to Naver Clip: 
        * <https://tv.naver.com/v/19961840> -> <https://m.naver.com/shorts/>
        * <https://tv.naver.com/embed/19961840> -> <https://m.naver.com/shorts/oembed/>
     3. The Naver Sports video page still loads: <https://m.sports.naver.com/video/19961840>  
(it redirects to <https://m.sports.naver.com/video/19961840/sports>).  
In the browser, this page requests video metadata from a new endpoint:  
GET <https://api-gw.sports.naver.com/video/19961840>  
I did not check whether that response contains the stream URLs.
     4. The front-end bundle path of the sports video page contains a build stamp "261022-..."  
(<https://ssl.pstatic.net/static.sports/resources/sports-web/video/261022-144423-45/>...),  
which matches the timing: downloads worked on 2026-10-21 and fail afterwards.

So the old play-info path used by the NaverTV extractor (now_web2) seems to be retired,  
and Naver Sports videos may need a new extractor based on the api-gw.sports.naver.com endpoint  
(or on Naver Clip).

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

On specific twitter posts, yt-dlp attempts to download a nonexistant video (where there is a single video, but yt-dlp attempts to download a second) and fails because of missing formulas. There is one video in the following twitter post: `https://x.com/lunncrf/status/2067551449538560394`, but `yt-dlp` attempts and fails to download a second. Running again with the `-J` option for debugging purposes yields a `null` in the array of playlist entries. No authentication is necessary for this particular tweet, and supplying cookies does not change the behavior in this instance.

# Question: Mitigating YouTube live-stream download interruption when a stream briefly goes offline #17883

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Open

Open

[Question: Mitigating YouTube live-stream download interruption when a stream briefly goes offline](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17883#top)#17883

Copy link

Labels

[questionQuestion](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22question%22)Question

## Description

[](https://github.com/zoriamon)

[zoriamon](https://github.com/zoriamon)

opened [on Oct 21, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17883#issue-5965064005)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

When a Youtube live-stream goes offline for a short period of time, for example if the streamer's internet drops or OBS plays up or they restart their computer, the stream will temporarily go offline. The stream itself hasn't ended, it has only gone offline.

My worst nightmare finally happened today that a video I was downloading was set to Private on its end, it went briefly offline but I forgot to check if yt-dlp was still going. My downloaded file was only the first 20 minutes of the 2 hour stream, unable to download the archived video.

`--socket-timeout SECONDS Time to wait before giving up, in seconds`  
There is no way to know how long a stream would go offline for to be able to put in a number of seconds, but would this be my best option?  
Could there be an option to ask if the stream has truly ended or is simply offline waiting for user input so yt-dlp can end or wait?

From my outside understanding, if the streamer hasn't turned off the stream in Youtube Studio the channel/stream room is still open but data isn't being received to stream, thus offline not ended. Sometimes when a streamer forgets to properly end the stream like this live-chat is left in limbo and the comment section below is not opened up on a page refresh.  
Is there no way for yt-dlp to wait properly for a stream to end, i.e. when the connection is severed from the streamer's side and the Youtube end card/suggested videos screen shows, so that there is no worry when a stream goes offline that yt-dlp will see no data and begin to mux?

I am not adding a verbose output as it's unnecessary.

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

A followup to [#16877](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16877), I guess.

Previous mechanisms for obtaining the `loid` token appear to still work, with the caveat that the `token_v2` cookie may now additionally be required (however, these mechanisms simply grab all of the cookies that reddit sets, so that isn't a problem).

However, starting sometime recently, even with all the cookies set, the url that is supposed to give the JSON for a post now shows a "You've been blocked by network security." page — even when navigating from a browser (I use firefox). Navigating to the actual reddit page still works though.

Like I mentioned in the linked issue, I'm connecting from a domestic IP and I don't hammer reddit with downloads very much, so I'm making this issue to see if other people are/will soon start experiencing this. If this starts becoming widespread, we'll/you'll need to look for a fix. Maybe trudging through the javascript could be fruitful (having to start extracting the information from the HTML would be rather yikes, certainly). And if this simply goes away and doesn't come back I'll just close the issue.

  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

This looks like some form of bot detection, with some initial state data not being sent when yt-dlp request the page. It seems to be pretty aggressive though: I have the same problem when trying to view anything in Firefox, there the page source is missing the same data and I get redirected to a 404 error page. In contrast, in chrome the video plays just fine for me and has the initial state as expected. Impersonate does not seem to do anything for me, unfortunately.

On second thought, there is more going on here. Adding a language code to the path segment (i.e. <https://www.bilibili.com/en/video/BV1kh4y1Y7Ko>) makes it work in browser, and then presumably also would make it work given the fix proposed in [#17879](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17879). So these two issues are closely related.

Hi I think I have found a workaround that worked for me  
So I initially attempted using the `/en/video/` URL but it failed with the generic extractor and an `html` extension error.  
Then I tried with cookie, by ysing the standard `/video/` URL with Chrome cookies. It successfully downloaded and merged the video:
         
         yt-dlp --cookies-from-browser chrome "<standard Bilibili video URL>"

Let me know if that helps!

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I am trying to download a season of a series from the ZDF Mediathek, for example `https://www.zdf.de/serien/die-bergretter-104?staffel=2`. This used to work in the past (a few months ago) but now isn't working anymore. I assume that some part of the ZDF API changed in the meantime.

Apparently, yt-dlp can't find the season information in the data returned by the API, and therefore can't list all the episodes of the season. Attempting to download a single episode from the season with the direct link to the episode works just fine.

Edit: This seems to only happen with some series. For example, `https://www.zdf.de/serien/extraordinary-100?staffel=2` works fine, i.e., the episodes are found. But it appears that either all seasons of a series work, or no seasons of a series work.

  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

United States

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

### Description

Tumblr extractor fails with `HTTP Error 403: Forbidden` on public posts when downloading webpage. Passing `--cookies-from-browser` does not resolve the issue.

### Probable Cause

In `yt_dlp/extractor/tumblr.py` (lines ~420–422), `_real_extract` formats URLs as ￹`http://{blog}.tumblr.com/post/{video_id}` and sends `headers={'User-Agent': 'WhatsApp/2.0'}`.  
Tumblr now returns HTTP 403 Forbidden with a challenge cookie (`_hcc`) for that User-Agent on subdomain endpoints.

### Possible Solution

Change the target URL in `_real_extract` to `https://www.tumblr.com/{blog}/{video_id}` with standard headers.  
The ￹existing `api_only` / `_ACCESS_TOKEN` flow already handles any login redirects and successfully retrieves the media ￹metadata via the permalink API.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

Using Windows Python 3.15.2 and `pyinstaller==6.22.0`, I can reproduce the issue with `curl-cffi==0.17.0` but I **cannot** reproduce the issue with `curl-cffi==0.16.3`.

Comparing the PyInstaller logs from each run, I see this warning only in the `curl-cffi==0.17.0` log:
         
         14383 WARNING: Library not found: could not resolve 'python3t.dll', dependency of 'D:\\a\\testing\\testing\\.venv\\Lib\\site-packages\\curl_cffi\\_wrapper.pyd'.
         

It looks like the curl-cffi 0.17.0 wrapper library (`_wrapper.pyd`) is linking to the free-threaded (GIL-disabled) CPython library (`python3t.dll`). We're building with GIL-enabled CPython, so PyInstaller can't find `python3t.dll` to include it in the bundle, and it bundles a broken curl-cffi library which silently errors when yt-dlp tries to import it.

What do we do about this? Dunno yet. Not sure if this is a PyInstaller issue, a curl-cffi issue, a CPython issue, or some combination.

👍React with 👍1Reacted by nicolaasjan

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Australia

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

  * Debian 13, Chrome cookies via `--cookies-from-browser chrome+gnomekeyring`.
  * Cookies extracted successfully: approximately 302 cookies.
  * Reproduced after updating to nightly `2026.10.29.232701`.
  * Example command: 
        
        yt-dlp --cookies-from-browser chrome+gnomekeyring "https://www.instagram.com/reels/DMNvOGvIzEU/"

  * Error: 
        
        Failed to parse JSON (caused by JSONDecodeError("Expecting value in '': line 1 column 1 (char 0)"))
        

  * `--write-pages` captured a **795,635-byte HTML document beginning`<!DOCTYPE html>`**, containing Instagram Home/navigation content—not an empty response or malformed JSON.
  * The reel remained playable in the logged-in browser.
  * Changing User-Agent and trying Chrome impersonation did not resolve it.



NOTE: This report concerns Instagram Reels specifically, rather than Stories. The three suggested potential duplicates concern Stories; I have not established whether they share the same underlying cause.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Region

United States

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

yt-dlp's stable and master releases are no longer working with Facebook Videos. I have confirmed this by dumping the page and reviewing the data. I am not hitting a checkpoint or anything of that nature.

Stack trace (Sentry): <https://ccallahanops.sentry.io/share/issue/4a00b3e6bc4047c58992b180f766961b/>

I will add that this may be just now rolling out, as my connection from the Central US has no issues, but on the east coast I have multiple servers having issues.

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

> What are you trying to do?

I was trying to change the `duration` field to try to bypass [this website](https://ytdlp.online)'s ban on really long videos which (as revealed by running a `-v` and looking at `[debug] Command-line config: `) seems to be enforced by adding `--print "pre_process:YTDLP_DURATION:%(duration)j"` and then checking for said line via whatever is wrapping yt-dlp itself (though they could have just put `--match-filters "duration<[whatever max duration num]"` at the end...).

This "usecase" probably does not matter at all for the purposes of this project; I just wanted to report this when I found it as it seemed like a bug. Judging by how you removed the `bug` label, is this somehow intended behavior?

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

A recent post by a creator I support on Patreon has two videos attached to it. One is the main post video that shows at the top of the page, the second is embedded into the content of the page. This embedded video also uses the 'built-in' Patreon video embed and provider - it is not a YT or Vimeo embed. When YT-DLP is pointed at the post it only detects the first 'primary' video, not the second video in the content.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

Investigating how the extractor works, I looked into the API response for the post in question, and found that the `content` field for the post was empty. By issuing a request without the field parameters YT-DLP normally applies to the request I was able to get the full response for the post (attached below). This has the content for the post as an embedded JSON string in the `content_json_string` parameter as an embedded JSON string. This embedded JSON can be decoded to find the `media_id` for the video that YT-DLP fails to detect.

[172527548.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33746528/172527548.json)

### Region

_No response_

### Example URLs

<https://kaiielle.com/posts/ted-lasso-pilot-156611354>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Patreon allows for creators to [attach a custom domain](https://support.patreon.com/hc/en-gb/articles/40759159136525-Connect-a-custom-domain-to-your-Patreon) to their Patreon account. Once set up Patreon serves their profile and posts under that custom domain rather than under `www.patreon.com/creator-name` \- as such, the Patreon extractor no longer matches the URLs and extraction falls back to the generic extractor, which fails due to how Patreon media and embeds need to be handled

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

  4. ### exterrestris commented on Oct 28, 2026

[](/exterrestris)

[exterrestris](/exterrestris)

[on Oct 28, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17940#issuecomment-6458952732)

ContributorAuthor

More actions

After looking into implementing a way for the generic extractor to detect a custom Patreon domain, that doesn't seem possible. The generic extractor needs to redirect back to the appropriate Patreon extractor to handle the actual extraction when a custom domain is detected, however yt-dlp will recheck that URL is valid for the new extractor. Unless the valid URLs on the Patreon extractors are made very generic - which will likely break other extractors, since the valid URLs would need to match any domain - the new extractor will be skipped as unsuitable.

Member

This PR will merge many features from <https://github.com/animelover1984/youtube-dl>  
Related: [animelover1984/youtube-dl#18](https://github.com/animelover1984/youtube-dl/issues/18)

### Features added:

  * [VideoRemuxer] Conditionally remux video
  * [VideoRemuxer] Add `-movflags +faststart` when remuxing from mp4
  * Write playlist data to infojson
  * [avanto] Use NFLTokenGenerator if possible
  * [ffmpeg] Print entire stderr in verbose when there is error
  * [ffmpeg] Handle URL filenames correctly
  * [ffmpeg] Warn when embedding ass in mp4
  * [FFmpegMetadata] Embed infojson inside the video
  * [embedthumbnail] Treat mka like mkv and mov like mp4
  * [embedthumbnail] Try embedding in mp4 using ffprobe and `-disposition`
  * [embedthumbnail] Embed in ogg/opus
  * [billibilli] Better video extraction
  * [billibilli] Extract comments
  * [billibilli] Added BiliBiliSearchIE, BilibiliChannelIE
  * [youtube] comment extraction



### Features not added:

  * Improvements to niconico - Meeds python 3.5+
  * [billibilli] Danmaku to subtitles - Licenced under GPL3
  * Split video by chapters - [@femaref](https://github.com/femaref) has a more updated [implementation](https://github.com/femaref/youtube-dl/tree/split-track)
  * rtmp fix - RTMP is outdated anyway. No point in trying to fix it



* * *

PS: I haven't tested a lot of this code yet. Will do it before merging

[@bbepis](https://github.com/bbepis) Please go though this and confirm whether you are willing to provide all of this code under Unlicence. I would appreciate it if you could also review the code

[@pukkandan](https://github.com/pukkandan)  
After reconsideration you have permission to take everything from the repo under Unlicense, including the comment downloading code. Note that there are still some issues with it and currently has a roughly 6000 comment cap, which I've yet to determine the fix for I think it would be mutually beneficial if you were to receive features that I implement from now on. I've realized I became the thing that I was so adamant against [@Jules-A](https://github.com/Jules-A)  
`-a batch-list.txt` is what downloads from line-separated links in a file. `--download-archive archive.txt` records the video IDs of every video you've downloaded, such that anything listed in the file is never redownloaded again. It's useful in your situation because it ignores the extension of already downloaded videos

# EJS

Jump to bottom

VXsz edited this page Jul 12, 2026 · [6 revisions](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/EJS/_history)

# External JS Scripts Setup Guide

To download from YouTube, yt-dlp needs to solve JavaScript challenges presented by YouTube using an external JavaScript runtime.

This involves running challenge solver scripts maintained at [yt-dlp-ejs](https://github.com/yt-dlp/ejs). Depending on your yt-dlp installation method, you may need to set up and enable these components manually. You will also have to install a supported JavaScript Runtime.

This guide will help you set up and enable the necessary components based on your yt-dlp installation method.

Note

EJS replaces the prior JSInterp and PhantomJS based approach. For YouTube both are no longer used. PhantomJS is still being used for a few other extractors, but is planned to be deprecated in the near future.

## Setup steps

  1. Install a supported JavaScript runtime
  2. Install EJS challenge solver scripts (yt-dlp-ejs)



## Step 1: Install a supported JavaScript Runtime

JS Runtime | Summary  
---|---  
Deno (recommended) | Enabled by default.  
Node | Enable with `--js-runtimes node`  
QuickJS | Enable with `--js-runtimes quickjs`  
Bun (deprecated) | Enable with `--js-runtimes bun`  
  
The JavaScript runtime executable should be located within your `PATH` (or located in the same folder as your `yt-dlp.exe` if you are on Windows). Otherwise, you'll need to specify the path to the JS runtime executable (or its containing folder) in your `--js-runtimes` argument, e.g.:
    
    
    --js-runtimes "deno:/path/to/deno"
    

### deno

Tip

Recommended

<https://deno.com>

#### Installation instructions

Minimum supported version: `2.3.0`

Download from <https://docs.deno.com/runtime/getting_started/installation/> or from your package manager.

When grabbing deno manually from the [Github release assets](https://github.com/denoland/deno/releases/latest) you will need to download `deno` and not `denort`.

#### Enable

Deno is enabled by default. To supply an optional path, use `--js-runtimes deno:/path/to/deno`

#### Notes

  * Code is run with restricted permissions (e.g, no file system or network access)
  * Supports downloading EJS script dependencies (yt-dlp-ejs) from [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/) (`--remote-components ejs:npm`).



* * *

### node

<https://nodejs.org>

#### Installation instructions

Minimum supported version: `22.0.0`

Download from <https://nodejs.org/en/download/> or from your package manager.

#### Enable

Enable with `--js-runtimes node` or `--js-runtimes node:/path/to/node`.

It is recommended to add this to your [yt-dlp configuration file](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp?tab=readme-ov-file#configuration) to avoid needing to pass it every time.

#### Notes

  * Runs code with [_some_ permissions restricted](https://nodejs.org/api/permissions.html).



* * *

### bun

<https://bun.com>

Warning

Support for `bun` is deprecated!

Versions after `1.3.14` are not supported, and support may be dropped entirely in the future.

#### Installation instructions

Minimum supported version: `1.2.11`

Latest supported version: `1.3.14`

Download from <https://bun.com/docs/installation> or from your package manager.

#### Enable

Enable with `--js-runtimes bun` or `--js-runtimes bun:/path/to/bun`.

It is recommended to add this to your [yt-dlp configuration file](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp?tab=readme-ov-file#configuration) to avoid needing to pass it every time.

#### Notes

  * No permission restrictions available. Scripts have full file system and network access.
  * Supports downloading EJS script dependencies (yt-dlp-ejs) from [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/) (`--remote-components ejs:npm`).
  * No support for SOCKS proxies when downloading EJS script dependencies from npm.



* * *

### QuickJS / QuickJS-NG

<https://bellard.org/quickjs/> / <https://quickjs-ng.github.io/quickjs/>

#### Installation instructions

Minimum supported QuickJS version: `2023-12-9`

All versions of QuickJS-NG are supported.

Download from <https://bellard.org/quickjs/> / <https://quickjs-ng.github.io/quickjs/installation> or from your package manager.

#### Enable

Enable with `--js-runtimes quickjs` or `--js-runtimes quickjs:/path/to/qjs`.

It is recommended to add this to your [yt-dlp configuration file](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp?tab=readme-ov-file#configuration) to avoid needing to pass it every time.

#### Notes

  * QuickJS versions prior to `2025-4-26` are missing optimizations which can lead to execution times of several minutes.
  * QuickJS-NG versions prior to `0.12.0` are missing optimizations which can lead to execution times of several minutes.
  * Both QuickJS and QuickJS-NG do not fully allow executing files from stdin, so yt-dlp will create temporary files for each EJS script execution. This can theoretically lead to time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) vulnerabilities.
  * The filename of the executable must be `qjs` (or `qjs.exe` on Windows), or else the path to _the executable file_ must be specified in the `--js-runtimes` argument.



## Step 2: Install EJS challenge solver scripts (yt-dlp-ejs)

yt-dlp distribution | EJS scripts installation options  
---|---  
Official PyInstaller-bundled executable (e.g. `yt-dlp.exe`, `yt-dlp_macos`, `yt-dlp_linux`, etc) | No additional action required. `yt-dlp-ejs` is bundled with these executables.  
PyPI package (e.g. installed with pip, pipx, etc): | \- Install and upgrade yt-dlp with `default` dependency group  
\- or enable npm downloads (deno/bun only)  
\- or enable GitHub downloads  
  
Official zipimport binary (the `yt-dlp` Unix executable) | No additional action required. `yt-dlp-ejs` is bundled with these executables.  
Third-party package users (e.g. installed with pacman, brew, etc) | This will depend on if your third-party package repository ships or bundles the EJS script package (`yt-dlp-ejs`) with yt-dlp.  
  
If it does not (or it is out of date):   
\- enable npm downloads (deno/bun only)   
\- or enable GitHub downloads  
  
  
### Option 1: Install the yt-dlp-ejs python package

yt-dlp ships a companion package, `yt-dlp-ejs`, which contains all the EJS scripts.

If you installed yt-dlp using the PyPI package (e.g. with pip or pipx), install _and upgrade_ yt-dlp with the `default` dependency group:

i.e. `pip install -U "yt-dlp[default]"`

The default dependency group includes the `yt-dlp-ejs` package.

Refer to <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Installation#with-pip> for more details.

Alternatively, if you only want to install the EJS package, you can install the `yt-dlp-ejs` package directly from PyPI. The version MUST match the version specified in yt-dlp's `pyproject.toml` for the version of yt-dlp you are using.

Warning

This library SHOULD be updated alongside yt-dlp to avoid running an outdated version. The version MUST be a supported version as per yt-dlp's pyproject.toml file. yt-dlp may bump the minimum version on updates without warning, and old versions will be ignored by yt-dlp.

### Option 2: Enable EJS script downloads from npm

Important

This option only works with Deno and Bun runtimes, which support downloading npm packages on-the-fly.

To enable this, supply `--remote-components ejs:npm` to yt-dlp. It is recommended to add this to your [yt-dlp configuration file](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp?tab=readme-ov-file#configuration) to avoid needing to pass it every time and allow automatic updates.

### Option 3: Enable EJS script downloads from GitHub

yt-dlp can automatically download the EJS scripts directly from GitHub (<https://github.com/yt-dlp/ejs>).

To enable this, supply `--remote-components ejs:github` to yt-dlp. It is recommended to add this to your [yt-dlp configuration file](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp?tab=readme-ov-file#configuration) to avoid needing to pass it every time and allow automatic updates.

Note

This method may not work if GitHub and GitHub release assets are not accessible from your network. This includes if you are using yt-dlp with an IPv6 IP-only (e.g., `--force-ipv6`)

## Plugins

You can install alternatives to `yt-dlp-ejs` through plugins.

### Featured Plugins:

  * [yt-dlp-apple-webkit-jsi](https://github.com/grqz/yt-dlp-apple-webkit-jsi) by [grqz](https://github.com/grqz)
    * Experimental Apple WebKit JS Challenge Provider plugin for yt-dlp. Should work on most Apple devices. _Maintained by a yt-dlp maintainer_



Check out the [yt-dlp-jsc-provider](https://github.com/topics/yt-dlp-jsc-provider) GitHub topic for more JSC Provider plugins.

For developers, refer to the [JSC Provider developer documentation](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/jsc/README.md)

  * **Please note: Currently only the base JavaScript Challenge Provider API is public. The API to hook into yt-dlp's EJS scripts is private at this time due to ongoing development with potential breaking changes; it may be made public in the future.**

#  `--exec` command injection when using `%q` in yt-dlp on Windows (CVE-2023-40581 bypass) 

High 

[Grub4K](/Grub4K) published GHSA-hjq6-52gw-2g7p Apr 9, 2024

## Package

pip yt-dlp ([pip](/advisories?query=ecosystem%3Apip)) 

## Affected versions

>=2021.04.11, <2024.04.09

## Patched versions

2024.04.09

## Description

### Summary

The [patch that addressed CVE-2023-40581](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/de015e930747165dbb8fcd360f8775fd973b7d6e) attempted to prevent RCE when using `--exec` with `%q` by replacing double quotes with two double quotes.  
However, this escaping is not sufficient, and still allows expansion of environment variables.

Support for output template expansion in `--exec`, along with this vulnerable behavior, was added to `yt-dlp` in version [2021.04.11](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/releases/tag/2021.04.11).
    
    
    > yt-dlp "https://youtu.be/42xO6rVqf2E" --ignore-config -f 18 --exec "echo %(title)q"
    [youtube] Extracting URL: https://youtu.be/42xO6rVqf2E
    [youtube] 42xO6rVqf2E: Downloading webpage
    [youtube] 42xO6rVqf2E: Downloading ios player API JSON
    [youtube] 42xO6rVqf2E: Downloading android player API JSON
    [youtube] 42xO6rVqf2E: Downloading m3u8 information
    [info] 42xO6rVqf2E: Downloading 1 format(s): 18
    [download] Destination: %CMDCMDLINE：~-1%&echo pwned&calc.exe [42xO6rVqf2E].mp4
    [download] 100% of  126.16KiB in 00:00:00 at 2.46MiB/s
    [Exec] Executing command: echo "%CMDCMDLINE:~-1%&echo pwned&calc.exe"
    ""
    pwned

### Patches

yt-dlp version 2024.04.09 fixes this issue by properly escaping `%`. It replaces them with `%%cd:~,%`, a variable that expands to nothing, leaving only the leading percent.

### Workarounds

It is recommended to upgrade yt-dlp to version 2024.04.09 as soon as possible. Also, always be careful when using `--exec`, because while this specific vulnerability has been patched, using unvalidated input in shell commands is inherently dangerous.

For Windows users who are not able to upgrade:

  * Avoid using any output template expansion in `--exec` other than `{}` (filepath).
  * If expansion in `--exec` is needed, verify the fields you are using do not contain `%`, `"`, `|` or `&`.
  * Instead of using `--exec`, write the info json and load the fields from it instead.



### Details

When escaping variables, the following code is used for Windows.  
[`yt_dlp/compat/__init__.py` line 31-33](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/8e6e3651727b0b85764857fc6329fe5e0a3f00de/yt_dlp/compat/__init__.py#L31-L33)
    
    
        def compat_shlex_quote(s):
            import re
            return s if re.match(r'^[-_\w./]+$', s) else s.replace('"', '""').join('""')

It replaces `"` with `""` to balance out the quotes and keep quoting intact if non-allowed characters are included. However, the `%CMDCMDLINE%` variable can be used to generate a quote using `%CMDCMDLINE:~-1%`; since the value of `%CMDCMDLINE%` is the commandline with which `cmd.exe` was called, and it is always called with the command surrounded by quotes, `%CMDCMDLINE:~-1%` expands to `"`. After the quotes have been unbalanced, special characters are no longer quoted and commands can be executed:
    
    
    %CMDCMDLINE:~-1%&calc.exe

  * <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-22423>

#  Arbitrary command injection with the `--netrc-cmd` option in yt-dlp 

High 

[Grub4K](/Grub4K) published GHSA-g3gw-q23r-pgqm Feb 21, 2026

## Package

pip yt-dlp ([pip](/advisories?query=ecosystem%3Apip)) 

## Affected versions

>=2023.06.21, <2026.02.21

## Patched versions

>=2026.02.21

## Description

### Summary

When yt-dlp's `--netrc-cmd` command-line option (or `netrc_cmd` Python API parameter) is used, an attacker could achieve arbitrary command injection on the user's system with a maliciously crafted URL.

### Impact

We assume the impact of this vulnerability to be high for anyone who uses `--netrc-cmd` in their command/configuration or `netrc_cmd` in their Python scripts. Even though the maliciously crafted URL itself will look very suspicious to many users, it would be trivial for a maliciously crafted webpage with an inconspicuous URL to covertly exploit this vulnerability via HTTP redirect. Users without `--netrc-cmd` in their arguments or `netrc_cmd` in their scripts are unaffected. No evidence has been found of this exploit being used in the wild.

### Patches

yt-dlp version 2026.02.21 fixes this issue by validating all netrc "machine" values and raising an error upon unexpected input.

### Workarounds

It is recommended to upgrade yt-dlp to version 2026.02.21 as soon as possible.

Users who are unable to upgrade should avoid using the `--netrc-cmd` command-line option (or `netrc_cmd` Python API parameter), or they should at least not pass a placeholder (`{}`) in their `--netrc-cmd` argument.

### Details

yt-dlp's `--netrc-cmd` option can be used to run any arbitrary shell command to retrieve site login credentials so that the user doesn't have to store the credentials as plaintext in the filesystem. The `--netrc-cmd` argument is a shell command with an optional placeholder (`{}`). If the placeholder is present in the argument, it is replaced with the netrc "machine" value, which specifies the site for which login credentials are needed.

The netrc "machine" value is usually explicitly defined in yt-dlp's extractor code for a given site. However, yt-dlp has four extractors where the netrc "machine" value needs to be dynamically sourced from the site's hostname. And in three of those extractors (`GetCourseRuIE`, `TeachableIE` and `TeachableCourseIE`), wildcard matches are allowed for one or more subdomains of the hostname. This can result in a netrc "machine" value that contains special shell characters.

The `--netrc-cmd` argument is executed by a modified version of Python's `subprocess.Popen` with `shell=True`, which means that any special characters may be interpreted by the host shell, potentially leading to arbitrary command injection.

Here is an example of maliciously crafted URL input that exploits the vulnerability:
    
    
    > yt-dlp --netrc-cmd "echo {}" "https://;echo pwned>&2;#.getcourse.ru/video"
    [GetCourseRu] Executing command: echo getcourseru
    WARNING: [GetCourseRu] Failed to parse .netrc: bad toplevel token 'getcourseru' (-, line 2)
    [GetCourseRu] Extracting URL: https://;echo pwned>&2;#.getcourse.ru/video
    [GetCourseRu] Executing command: echo ;echo pwned>&2;
    pwned
    [GetCourseRu] No authenticators for ;echo pwned>&2;
    [GetCourseRu] video: Downloading webpage

Although only 3 of yt-dlp's extractors are directly susceptible to this attack, yt-dlp's "generic" extractor will follow HTTP redirects and try to match the resulting URL with one of the dedicated extractors. This means that any URL processed by the generic extractor could ultimately lead to a maliciously crafted URL that is matched by one of the vulnerable extractors. Hypothetically, an attacker could create a website with an inconspicuous URL and legitimate-looking media content that would serve an HTTP redirect to a maliciously crafted URL when it detects a request from yt-dlp.

#  Generic Extractor MITM Vulnerability via Arbitrary Proxy Injection 

Moderate 

[Grub4K](/Grub4K) published GHSA-3ch3-jhc6-5r8x Nov 14, 2023

## Package

pip yt-dlp ([pip](/advisories?query=ecosystem%3Apip)) 

## Affected versions

>=2022.10.04

## Patched versions

2023.11.14

## Description

### Impact

The Generic Extractor in yt-dlp is vulnerable to an attacker setting an arbitrary proxy for a request to an arbitrary url, allowing the attacker to MITM the request made from yt-dlp's HTTP session. This could lead to cookie exfiltration in some cases.

Details

To pass extra control data between extractors (such as headers like `Referer`), yt-dlp employs a concept of "url smuggling". This works by adding this extra data as json to the url fragment ("smuggling") that is then passed on to an extractor. The receiving extractor then "unsmuggles" the data from the input url. This functionality is intended to be internal only.

Currently, the Generic extractor supports receiving an arbitrary dictionary of HTTP headers in a smuggled url, of which it extracts and adds them to the initial request it makes to such url. This is useful when a url sent to the Generic extractor needs a `Referer` header sent with it, for example.

Additionally, yt-dlp has internal headers to set a proxy for a request: `Ytdl-request-proxy` and `Ytdl-socks-proxy`. While these are deprecated, internally `Ytdl-request-proxy` is still used for `--geo-verification-proxy`.

However, it is possible for a maliciously crafted site include these smuggled options in a url which then the Generic extractor extracts and redirects to itself. This allows a malicious website to **set an arbitrary proxy for an arbitrary url that the Generic extractor will request.**

This could allow for the following, but not limited too:

  * An attacker can MITM a request it asks yt-dlp to make to **any** website. 
    * If a user has loaded cookies into yt-dlp for the target site, which are not marked as [secure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secure_cookie), they could be exfiltrated by the attacker.
    * Fortunately most sites are HTTPS and should be setting cookies as secure.
  * An attacker can set cookies for an arbitrary site.



An example malicious webpage:
    
    
    <!DOCTYPE html>
    <cinerama.embedPlayer('t','{{ target_site }}#__youtubedl_smuggle=%7B%22http_headers%22:%7B%22Ytdl-request-proxy%22:%22{{ proxy url }}%22%7D,%22fake%22:%22.smil/manifest%22%7D')

Where `{{ target_site }}` is the URL Generic extractor will request and `{{ proxy url }}` is the proxy to proxy the request for this url through.

### Patches

  * We have removed the ability to smuggle `http_headers` to the Generic extractor, as well as other extractors that use the same pattern.



### Workarounds

  * Disable Generic extractor (`--ies default,-generic`), or only pass trusted sites with trusted content.
  * Take caution when using `--no-check-certificate`.

  * [GHSA-3ch3-jhc6-5r8x](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-3ch3-jhc6-5r8x "GHSA-3ch3-jhc6-5r8x")
  * <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-46121>

#  CVSS v3 base metrics 

Attack vector: More severe the more the remote (logically and physically) an attacker can be in order to exploit the vulnerability.

Attack complexity: More severe for the least complex attacks.

Privileges required: More severe if no privileges are required.

User interaction: More severe when no user interaction is required.

Scope: More severe when a scope change occurs, e.g. one vulnerable component impacts resources in components beyond its security scope.

Confidentiality: More severe when loss of data confidentiality is highest, measuring the level of data access available to an unauthorized user.

Integrity: More severe when loss of data integrity is the highest, measuring the consequence of data modification possible by an unauthorized user.

Availability: More severe when the loss of impacted component availability is highest.
